overall: Tomorrow (Sunday, June 28) in Washington, DC will be a warm, mostly cloudy day with lingering morning fog and scattered rain showers before 2pm, transitioning to scattered thunderstorms in the afternoon. Conditions will remain unsettled with a 50% precipitation chance and a northeast wind around 7 mph keeping temperatures from reaching their full potential. It will be a muggy, active weather day with no significant severe weather threat locally, though a Flood Watch remains in effect for portions of east Tennessee through late morning.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model spread on tomorrow's high: ECMWF is a significant warm outlier at ~85.5°F (top bucket 88-89F), while the GFS (78.6°F), HRRR (82.3°F), NBM (82.0°F), and Weather.com (80.5°F) all cluster in the lower 79–83°F range, suggesting the ensemble's expected TMAX of 85.0°F is being pulled upward primarily by ECMWF. The majority of models lean toward a high in the low-to-mid 80s, broadly consistent with the NWS narrative forecast of near 84°F.
max_temp_prediction: The most likely TMAX for Sunday falls in the 83–85°F range, with the active Kalshi odd-bucket top at 83–84°F (25.2% probability) and the even-bucket peak at 84–85°F (47.5%). Clouds, morning fog, and scattered precipitation will act as a ceiling on daytime heating, making an extreme high unlikely and lending confidence to the mid-84°F target area. Confidence is moderate — the ECMWF outlier introduces upside risk toward the upper 80s, but the weight of model consensus and cloudy/rainy conditions argues for a high near 84°F.
